title: Integrated Access, Change, and Spend Governance
author: Anjali Rao
content:
Overview

Purpose:
This document defines Redwood Inference’s unified policies and operating procedures for access & permissions, change management, data stewardship, procurement & expenses, vendor management, and business travel. The goal is consistent, auditable decisions that balance speed of product development and the company’s risk profile.

Scope:
Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and third-party vendors who interact with company systems, data, procurement processes, or travel on behalf of Redwood. Exceptions must be approved by the applicable process owner (see Owners & Contacts).

Principles (short):
- Least privilege: default access is limited and granted for a stated business purpose.
- Separation of duties: request, approval, and execution should, where practical, be handled by different roles.
- Risk proportionality: controls scale with sensitivity of data or magnitude of spend.
- Auditability: all requests and approvals must leave an auditable trail.
- Minimal friction: templates and predefined workflows reduce decision latency for routine actions.

Owners & Contacts:
- Policy owner: Finance & Legal (policy oversight and procurement thresholds) — owner@redwood.ai
- Access & Permissions: Security & Compliance (RBAC, identity lifecycle) — iam@redwood.ai
- Change Management: Eng Platform (service deployments, infra changes) — eng-platform@redwood.ai
- Data Management: Data Governance (classification, retention) — data-gov@redwood.ai
- Travel & Expense Policy: People Ops + Finance — travel@redwood.ai
- Vendor Management: Procurement (onboarding & contracts) — procurement@redwood.ai

1) Access & Permissions (Identity and RBAC)

Overview:
Access to systems is controlled through centralized identity providers (IdP) and role-based access control (RBAC) groups. Temporary elevated access must use just-in-time (JIT) mechanisms with approval and expiry.

Account lifecycle:
1. New hire: People Ops generates onboarding ticket that triggers automated IdP account creation with baseline role.
2. Role change: Manager files role-change request; affected access is adjusted within 2 business days.
3. Offboarding: Access revoked within 4 hours of termination for company-managed devices; keys rotated.

Access request process:
- Requestor: Files an Access Request via the internal portal (link: /selfservice/access). Include business justification, owner of resource, and requested duration if temporary.
- Approver: Resource owner or designated approver reviews and approves/denies in 72 hours.
- Exceptions: Any permanent access requests for prod-sensitive systems require a security review.

Privilege classes and approval thresholds (table):
- Read-only non-sensitive (e.g., documentation): Manager approval.
- Read-write non-sensitive (e.g., dev infra repos): Team lead + change advisory notification.
- Prod access (read-only): Team lead + security reviewer.
- Prod access (write/exec): Team lead + engineering manager + security + audit logging enabled.

Just-in-time (JIT) escalation:
- JIT sessions limited to 4 hours by default. Longer durations require written justification and approval by Security + Eng Manager.

Periodic reviews:
- Quarterly access certification: Team managers receive list of active access for attestations. Remediation tickets created for stale access.

2) Change Management (Infra & Service Changes)

Purpose:
Ensure changes to production and shared infrastructure are planned, tested, and reversible while minimizing deployment friction for engineers.

Change categories and required controls:
- Standard changes (routine, documented, low risk): Pre-approved; must follow runbook. Example: rotating certificates on dev clusters.
- Significant changes (architecture or database schema changes impacting >1 service): Require design review + rollout plan + canary/A/B strategy + rollback plan.
- Emergency changes (incident mitigation): Follow incident change protocol; post-change RCA and retrospective required within 3 business days.

Change process (numbered steps):
1. Create a Change Request (CR) in the change tracker: title, owner, impact, roll-forward, rollback, test plan, monitoring, and list of services impacted.
2. Automated validations run: unit tests, static checks, dependency scan.
3. Review board (daily lightweight triage for non-urgent) evaluates Significant CRs.
4. Schedule and notify stakeholders at least 48 hours before planned change for Significant changes.
5. Execute during approved change window with live monitoring and a point of contact on call.
6. Document outcome and update runbooks or architecture docs.

Rollback and fail-forward guidance:
- Prefer automated rollbacks when possible.
- If a rollback is riskier than a fail-forward, document reasons and get change board concurrence.

3) Data Management (Classification, Handling, Retention)

Classification scheme:
- Public: Intended for public consumption. Low control.
- Internal: Company-internal operational data (e.g., standard docs).
- Confidential: Customer-facing PII or sensitive product telemetry.
- Restricted: Regulated data or high-risk intellectual property (e.g., model weights tied to customer IP).

Storage and access by classification:
- Public/Internal: Stored in general repositories; standard backups.
- Confidential: Access limited to vetted roles; encryption at rest; access logged.
- Restricted: Dedicated storage regions, customer-specific tenancy, mandatory data processing agreements, and periodic audit.

Data retention & deletion:
- Default retention: 24 months for logs; config and infra state retained for 36 months.
- Customer data: retention bound to contract; default retention 90 days unless longer required.
- Deletion: Use the Data Deletion Request template (see Templates). Data deletion requests create ticket and must be verified by Data Governance.

Data handling controls (examples):
- Secrets must never be checked into source control. Use the secrets manager (link: /internal/secrets).
- Analytics buckets containing Confidential data must have DLP policies and approved consumers list.

Data breach and incident response intersection:
- Any suspected exfiltration or misconfiguration that exposes Confidential or Restricted data must be reported immediately to security-incident@redwood.ai and follow the incident runbook.

4) Procurement & Expenses

Policy objectives:
Control company spend, ensure competitive vendor selection, and provide fast approvals for routine low-value purchases.

Approval matrix (simplified):
- <$1,000: Team lead approval.
- $1,000–$25,000: Department head + procurement notification.
- >$25,000: Procurement + Finance + Legal (requires budget code and contract review).

Preferred vendor and procurement steps:
1. For hardware, cloud commitments, or software licenses over $5,000, run a comparative vendor assessment (3 bids recommended).
2. Submit a Purchase Request (PR) in the procurement tool: include scope, estimated TCO, budget code, and preferred vendor.
3. Procurement verifies vendor compliance checks (security questionnaire, SOC reports if applicable).
4. Finance issues PO or processes contract after approval.

Expense reimbursements (employee travel & incidental):
- Submit receipts via the expense tool within 30 days.
- Per-diem and mileage rates are published in the Travel Appendix (see Templates).
- Non-compliant expenses (e.g., personal entertainment on company card) will be declined and remediated by People Ops + Finance.

Corporate cards and spend limits:
- Default corporate card limits are $3,000 per billing cycle; exceptions require Finance approval.
- Cardholders must reconcile transactions weekly and submit receipts within 7 days of purchase.

5) Vendor Management (Onboarding, Risk, and Contracting)

Onboarding checklist (minimum):
- Vendor risk assessment completed by Procurement.
- Security questionnaire and evidence (SOC2, encryption, incident history) if vendor will handle Confidential/Restricted data.
- Contractual terms: SLA, data protection addendum (DPA), liability and IP clauses, termination rights, and audit rights for critical vendors.
- Approved payment terms and PO issuance.

Vendor risk tiers and controls:
- Tier 1 (strategic/critical vendors): Quarterly reviews, contract >12 months, Exec sponsor, and enhanced security reviews.
- Tier 2 (operational vendors): Annual reviews, standard security attestations.
- Tier 3 (low-impact suppliers): Standard procurement process.

Vendor offboarding and data retrieval:
- Offboarding plan must include data return/destruction certificates, account closures, and revocation of any granted system access. Procurement coordinates with Security & Data Governance for verification.

6) Travel Policy (Business Travel, Safety, and Allowances)

Booking and approvals:
- Domestic travel under $1,500: Manager approval.
- International travel or bookings over $1,500: Manager + People Ops approval.
- Use the preferred travel portal (link: /travel/portal) for bookings to maintain corporate rates and traveler tracking.

Safety and emergency contact:
- Employees must register international travel in the traveler tracking system. The company provides emergency evacuation coverage where the country policy exists.

Per diems and allowable expenses:
- Lodging: reasonable single-occupancy rate; upgraded rooms require pre-approval.
- Meals: use per-diem tables or submit itemized receipts.
- Ground transport: rideshares & taxis accepted; car rentals require justification and additional insurer details.

Non-compliant travel items:
- First-class flights require People Ops + Exec approval.
- Personal side trips: expenses must be split and only business portion reimbursed.

7) Templates and Quick-Start Forms

Included templates (short description and usage):
- Purchase Request (PR) template: fields: requestor, department, budget code, description, justification, vendor options, estimated cost, impact.
- Access Request template: fields: requestor, resource, justification, duration, approver.
- Data Deletion Request: dataset identifier, owner, retention contract reference, deletion verification checklist.
- Change Request (CR) stub: summary, impacted services, rollback plan, monitoring queries, communication list.
- Travel Authorization form: itinerary, purpose, approver, estimated cost breakdown.

Sample: Purchase Request (PR) text snippet
```
Requestor: Anjali Rao
Department: Product
Budget Code: PROD-Q2-2026
Description: Annual license for test fleet management tool
Justification: Required for standardized benchmarking and fleet orchestration across Dedicated clusters
Estimated total: $18,750
Vendor options: Vendor A (preferred), Vendor B (backup)
Approvals: Team Lead -> Procurement -> Finance
```

Audit & Compliance

- All procurement and access logs retained for 36 months by default.
- Internal audits: Procurement & Finance run annual vendor audits; Security runs annual access audits and quarterly spot checks.
- Evidence retention for regulated contracts follows contract-specified retention terms (may exceed default retention).

Exception handling and policy updates

Exceptions:
- Temporary or one-off exceptions should be submitted to policy owner via the Exception Request template and include compensating controls and a defined expiry. Exceptions are time-boxed to 90 days unless renewed with justification.

Policy review cadence:
- Policy owner reviews this document annually or after any major regulatory change, merger, or incident.

Appendix: Quick references
- Access ticket portal: /selfservice/access
- Procurement tool: /tools/procure
- Secrets manager: /internal/secrets
- Traveler portal: /travel/portal
